reason: Pinned §4.1 delegates canonicalization to the package and the Python/Node byte divergence reproduces, but the clarification must preserve existing numeric and Unicode behavior before claiming JCS equivalence.
Explicit string-comparison rules would improve precision, but §4.1 already specifies capability-set comparison and the proposed empty-capability rejection adds a separate semantic change.
The stdin-framing asymmetry is real, but §9 already identifies requests exceeding 1 MiB as malformed and the proposed acceptance and EOF requirements need exceptions for invalid and oversized input.

A failed obsolete signature does not establish a disjoint signing key, and imposing one cryptographic evaluation sequence across all verifier classes exceeds the demonstrated denial-classification ambiguity.

§3.2 explicitly permits nonceless allows and §8 specifies returning presentation nullifiers, while a correctly operating local-mode verifier still burns nonces, so mandatory default rejection needs a clearer compatibility justification.
Pinned §3.4 accepts non-positive retention timestamps and no host rule compares them with now_unix, supporting bounded validation hardening with an additional elapsed-positive boundary case.
§7.3 already specifies inserting entry.nonce and §8 makes issuer_key bookkeeping-only, but an issuer-changing replay fixture would close a verified coverage gap.

Duplicate nonce entries are untested, but the claimed all-or-nothing reservation guarantee is absent and both pinned reference hosts deliberately retain novel nonces on conflicts, making the proposed rollback postcondition new behavior.

The published package is host-only, but the pinned repository already contains 10 external_verifier vectors including malformed stdin, so the candidate must narrow to uncovered envelope cases and reusable verifier invocation.

Adapter guidance could clarify policy denials, but pinned §9 already makes mechanism-specific meanings illustrative across classes and an informative note cannot silently impose mandatory detail fields.

The [Claude Code reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) confirms nonblocking command-hook failures and timeouts, but exit translation cannot repair failure of the wrapper itself, so the profile needs explicit runtime prerequisites.

Bundle opacity does not prohibit retaining an opaque bundle reference, §11 permits optional-field revisions under stated compatibility limits, and a profile-specific binding digest is not established as an EVC audit requirement.

The pinned IANA section already specifies Specification Required, registry columns, initial contents, and explicit wire-major registration restrictions, directly contradicting the alleged missing policy and unreconciled registry.

Pinned Appendix B is already explicitly informative with lowercase implementation requirements, so its proposed demotion addresses nonexistent normative scope while reference hygiene remains a narrower concern.
The pinned draft already contains Implementation Status, an RFC Editor removal note, and the external implementation's full commit and 27/27 coverage, leaving narrower URL and freshness corrections.

The pinned pseudocode omits schema, signal, and output-bound checks and checks exit status first; the diff should preserve SHOULD-level precedence and classify recorded streaming-bound kills instead of relying solely on post-wait length.

The [published specification](https://responsibleai.github.io/agent-hooks/spec/) already defines verdict validation, failure-to-deny mappings, and conformance, establishing substantial direct overlap and weakening the proposed easy adapter counter.

The [hook documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) confirms the transport fit and failure gap, but no receptive maintainer channel is evidenced and command-hook timeout remains an outer enforcement limitation.

Datatracker confirms an [active individual -12 draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-schrock-ep-authorization-receipts/), but its current authorization_binding design does not contain the cited mandate_id/scope_digest fields and adoption remains unverified.

The [active individual -10 draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-nelson-agent-delegation-receipts/) specifies narrowing-only delegation, supporting overlap and an adapter hypothesis, but its June update and unverified adoption limit momentum.

The pinned runner emits results without failure_class, the commands omit --type host_behavior and name the wrong Rust binary, and per-vector observation capture is required before this differential record is reproducible.
Pinned §§5.2–5.3 directly prohibit accepting this concrete stderr-only allow and no existing host fixture isolates it, making an additive vector with failure_class=unparseable_stdout straightforward.

Read-only sync:check confirms 32 vendored files and the existing MANIFEST match the pinned source, but the proposed record duplicates available hashes and does not establish equality with the published npm tarball.

Pinned history confirms exactly host-deny-unknown-denial-code and host-deny-signal-death-after-allow were added with prior inputs and expectations unchanged, supporting a historical coverage record that labels both untested and infers no new passes.
